discovery: Flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moiré quantum matter)

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moiré materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that at 'magic' twist angles the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this with experiments showing correlated insulating states and superconductivity near them in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This created a new and highly tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons. With a single gate one can move through phase diagrams like those of the cuprates, with nematicity, intertwined orders, orbital magnetism, Chern insulators, and later fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in related moiré systems. The work changed how the whole field approaches correlated quantum matter. It turned twist angle into a control parameter and let experiments test many theoretical ideas that had resisted clean tests for decades. It has been widely reproduced and extended across hundreds of laboratories, and its importance has proved durable.
